author: reek
body: alloc-bytes 0 advances the bump allocator by nothing and answers the current pointer, so a difference across a call is the bytes that call made permanent. The control row is the guard on the instrument: a loop that allocates nothing must read 0, and if it does not then nothing else measured here means anything.

author: reek
body: A bounded frame cost is not the same property as a bounded LOOP, and only the first of the two was ever asserted here. A view left open renders into one target over and over, so what decides whether it survives is what a frame leaves behind after the next one starts, not what one frame costs. These two run the same render the same number of times and differ only in the bracket.

author: reek
body: The unbracketed row is the control on the instrument. If it does not grow, the loop is not allocating and the bracketed row's flatness means nothing.
